Problems found
==============

1. Missing import  
   smtplib is used but never imported. The function will raise NameError.

2. Improper message construction  
   • RFC 5322 requires CRLF line breaks (“\r\n”), not “\n”.  
   • Building the message by string concatenation makes it easy to create malformed headers and breaks non-ASCII/UTF-8 bodies.  
   • The “To:” header is put in the message, but smtplib.sendmail receives a **different** recipient list. If you later pass several addresses separated by commas, the header will be wrong and some MTAs will treat each character as one address.  
   • No support for multipart, HTML, attachments, encoding, etc.

3. Header injection / e-mail spoofing  
   The values in to or subject can contain “\r” or “\n”:

       send_email('victim@example.com\nCc:other@evil.com', …)

   The injected header is sent verbatim because nothing validates or encodes it.

4. Lack of transport security & authentication  
   Unencrypted SMTP on port 25 is used; credentials are not sent, TLS is not started, and certificates are not verified. Anyone on the network (or any local user with access to the localhost SMTP proxy) can read or tamper with the mail.

5. Resource/exception handling  
   If an SMTP error occurs, quit() is never reached and the socket remains open. No error is logged or propagated.

6. Hard-coded addresses & magic values  
   Hard-coding “noreply@app.com” and “localhost” makes the function unusable in other environments and encourages address spoofing.

7. Non-ASCII headers & bodies  
   The code silently breaks if subject/body contain non-ASCII, because you did not declare an encoding.

8. Minor style issues  
   • Using variable name to (a built-in in other languages) is okay but “recipient” is clearer.  
   • Function returns nothing; callers have no idea whether the mail was delivered.

Recommended fix
---------------

Use the email package to build the message, validate inputs, use a context-manager for the connection, enable TLS, and handle errors explicitly.

```python
import re
import smtplib
from email.message import EmailMessage
from email.headerregistry import Address

# Very small e-mail validator – replace with something more robust if needed
EMAIL_RE = re.compile(r"^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$")

def _sanitise_address(addr: str) -> str:
    if '\r' in addr or '\n' in addr or not EMAIL_RE.match(addr):
        raise ValueError("Invalid e-mail address")
    return addr

def _sanitise_header(value: str, name: str = "header") -> str:
    if '\r' in value or '\n' in value:
        raise ValueError(f"Illegal characters in {name}")
    return value

def send_email(recipient, subject, body,
               smtp_host="smtp.example.com", smtp_port=587,
               from_addr="noreply@app.com",
               username=None, password=None, use_tls=True, timeout=10):
    """
    Send a text/plain e-mail.

    recipient can be a string or a list/tuple of strings.
    Raises ValueError on bad input and smtplib.SMTPException on transport errors.
    """
    # ----------  Input validation  ----------
    if isinstance(recipient, (list, tuple)):
        to_addrs = [_sanitise_address(a) for a in recipient]
    else:
        to_addrs = [_sanitise_address(recipient)]

    subject = _sanitise_header(subject, "Subject")

    # ----------  Build the message  ----------
    msg = EmailMessage()
    msg["From"] = from_addr
    msg["To"]   = ", ".join(to_addrs)
    msg["Subject"] = subject
    msg.set_content(body, charset="utf-8")

    # ----------  Send  ----------
    try:
        with smtplib.SMTP(smtp_host, smtp_port, timeout=timeout) as smtp:
            if use_tls:
                smtp.starttls()               # encrypted channel
            if username and password:
                smtp.login(username, password)
            smtp.send_message(msg, from_addr=from_addr, to_addrs=to_addrs)
    except smtplib.SMTPException as exc:
        # log or re-raise depending on your application
        raise
```

What this fixes / improves
--------------------------

• Uses EmailMessage → correct CRLF, MIME, non-ASCII handling, attachments possible later.  
• Eliminates header injection by rejecting “\r”/“\n” in headers and validating addresses.  
• Uses a context manager (`with … as smtp:`) so the connection is always closed.  
• Optional TLS and authentication.  
• Allows multiple recipients; header and envelope are kept in sync.  
• Accepts custom SMTP host/port; avoids hard-coding.  
• Explicit error propagation so callers know what happened.  
• UTF-8 body encoding by default.

Additional suggestions
----------------------

1. Replace the simple regex with a full e-mail validator (e.g., `email_validator` library).  
2. Log failures and maybe implement retry/back-off.  
3. If you send from an untrusted environment, pin the SMTP server’s certificate or use SMTPS (`smtplib.SMTP_SSL`).  
4. Consider rate-limiting / throttling calls to avoid accidental mail storms.
